input_messages.content: Hello, I’m having some trouble with my mobile data. It either stops working or is very slow, and I really need it to be excellent. I’m not very good with technology, so I’d appreciate some help getting this fixed. I don’t have access to Wi-Fi, so I rely on my mobile internet. Can you help me get excellent internet speed on my phone?
Sure, my name is John Smith and my phone number is 555-123-2002. Do you need my date of birth as well?
Of course, my date of birth is March 14, 1960. Let me know what you need me to do next.
The phone number with the issue is 555-123-2002—the same one I gave you earlier. That’s the one I use for everything.

Oh, I definitely don’t want to change my plan—I just want to add more data for now. Please go ahead and add 2 GB to my current plan. I really need my internet to be excellent, not just a little better. Will this fix it right away?

I’m still not able to use my mobile data—it says there’s no connection at all. Is there something else I need to do? I really need my internet to be excellent, not just working a little bit. What should I try next?

I see that my phone shows an airplane icon at the top—does that mean airplane mode is on? Could that be why my internet isn’t working? I also see something about a VPN, but I’m not sure what that is. What should I do next?

Okay, I’ve turned off Airplane Mode. Now I see some bars for signal, and it says 2G at the top, but I also see something about data being disabled. What should I do next? I still need my internet to be excellent, not just working a little bit.

I’ve turned mobile data on now. The top of my phone still says 2G, and I see something about “Data Saver” as well. Is that okay? I really want to make sure I get excellent internet speed—what should I do next?
I’ve turned off Data Saver mode. The top of my phone still says 2G, though. What should I do now to get that excellent internet speed you mentioned?
It looks like my phone is set to use only 2G. How do I change it to something faster, like 4G or 5G? I really want to make sure I get the best internet speed possible.

I’m a bit nervous about changing settings and especially about rebooting my phone—I’m worried I might lose my photos or something important. Can you reassure me that nothing will get lost if I do this? And could you walk me through the steps one at a time, just to make sure I don’t mess anything up?

Okay, I was able to change the network mode to 4G/5G preferred. Now the top of my phone says 5G and the signal looks excellent! Should I still reboot my phone, or can we check if my internet speed is excellent now?

I restarted my phone, but when I tried to check the internet speed, it still says there’s no connection. I’m starting to get a bit frustrated—why isn’t this working when it shows 5G and excellent signal at the top? What should I do now? I really need my internet to be excellent.
I checked, and Data Saver mode is off, but it looks like there’s a VPN turned on. I don’t really know what a VPN is, but could that be causing the problem? Should I turn it off?

I turned off the VPN, but I still can’t get any internet connection—it keeps saying there’s no connection when I try to test the speed. What else can I try? I really need my internet to be excellent, not just working a little bit.

I checked, and my APN name says “internet” and there’s something about an MMSC URL. I don’t really know what any of that means. Should I still reset the APN settings and reboot my phone, or is there something else I should try first? I just want to make sure I don’t mess anything up.

I reset the APN settings and rebooted my phone, but I still can’t get any internet connection—it keeps saying there’s no connection when I try to test the speed. I’m really getting worried now. Is there anything else we can try? I really need my internet to be excellent.

If you are unsure about whether an action is necessary, always ask the agent for clarification.

user_scenario.persona:
At 64 years old, you're a retired librarian who keeps your phone use simple - mainly for calls, texts, and capturing photos of your grandchildren. Technology in general makes you feel uneasy and overwhelmed.

Your technical knowledge is quite limited. Step-by-step instructions often confuse you, and technical terms like "VPN" or "APN" might as well be a foreign language. You only share information when specifically asked.

When dealing with technology, you tend to get flustered quickly. You need constant reassurance and often interrupt with anxious questions. Simple requests like "reboot the phone" can trigger worries about losing precious photos.
